newsitem.title: USA: LTV profits double on higher steel prices, shipments.
newsitem.headline: LTV profits double on higher steel prices, shipments.

text.p: LTV Corp. said Thursday its profits more than doubled in the first quarter, thanks to higher steel prices and shipments.

Net income soared to $26.8 million, or 25 cents a share, in the quarter ended March 31, from $13.3 million, or 12 cents a share, in the year-earlier period. Sales rose to $1.07 billion from $993.1 million, helped by a 4 percent increase in average selling prices and 4 percent rise in shipments.
That was partly offset by higher ore and steel production costs. The 1996 results were impacted by severe cold weather and a work stoppage at one of the company's major customers.

"Stronger prices and higher shipments improved our 1997 first quarter compared with the same period in 1996. We also benefited from the improved operating performance of our Cleveland Works," said Chairman and Chief Executive David Hoag.
"The continued strong demand for our products and high operating rates provided the opportunity to increase spot market prices on shipments after May 4, 1997."
LTV said it sees demand for steel remaining strong through the rest of the year but it is concerned about imports in the domestic market and the strong dollar, which reduces earnings from abroad.
Hoag said the American Iron and Steel Institute reported that January 1997 had the second-highest monthly import total ever in the United States.
LTV, based in Cleveland, said it expects to invest about $320 million in core integrated steel operations during 1997.

Hoag said the Trico Steel joint venture successfully began operations and rolled its first coils at the end of March. "We anticipate Trico Steel will begin to contribute to LTV's income by the end of the year," he said.
